questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: A quiz question asks: which proton type typically appears furthest downfield in a proton NMR spectrum?

options.misconception: alkyl methyls appear upfield near one ppm
vinyl protons appear near five to six ppm
aromatic protons appear near seven to eight ppm

questions.explanation: Carboxylic acid O-H protons are strongly deshielded and appear near ten to twelve ppm, further downfield than aromatic, vinyl or alkyl protons.
questions.hint: Acid O-H is the most deshielded common proton.

provenance.author: orgchem2-bank-author
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: For the sample reaction, a proton has two equivalent neighboring protons. How many lines does its signal show?

options.misconception: one neighbor gives a doublet
three neighbors give a quartet
no neighbors give a singlet

questions.explanation: Spin-spin coupling to n equivalent neighbors splits a signal into n plus one lines, so two equivalent neighbors give a triplet of three lines.
questions.hint: Two neighbors means n+1 equals three.

provenance.author: orgchem2-bank-author
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: During a lab exercise, which molecule gives exactly two signals in a proton-decoupled carbon-13 NMR spectrum?

options.misconception: pentane has three distinct carbon environments
isobutane has two carbon types with distinct methyl and methine
cyclohexane gives one carbon signal

questions.explanation: Neopentane has a central quaternary carbon and four equivalent methyl carbons, giving exactly two distinct carbon environments in the carbon-13 spectrum.
questions.hint: Symmetry reduces the number of distinct carbons.

provenance.author: orgchem2-bank-author
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: In a problem set, a signal integrates to six hydrogens while another integrates to one. What does the ratio indicate?

options.text: Six equivalent protons for that environment

options.misconception: integration counts protons, not environments
integration does not reveal ring size
that is determined by splitting, not integration

questions.explanation: The integral of a proton NMR signal is proportional to the number of protons giving that signal, so an integral of six corresponds to six equivalent protons.
questions.hint: Integration gives relative proton counts.

questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: Testing your understanding: which distinctive signal in a proton NMR spectrum indicates an aldehyde?

options.text: A broad signal near eleven ppm
options.misconception: that suggests a carboxylic acid O-H

options.text: A singlet near nine to ten ppm

options.misconception: that suggests a terminal methyl
that suggests aromatic protons

questions.explanation: The aldehydic proton is strongly deshielded by the carbonyl and typically appears as a singlet around nine to ten ppm, a region relatively empty for other protons.
questions.hint: Aldehyde protons sit near nine to ten ppm.

questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: A problem asks: in which region of a carbon-13 NMR spectrum does an ester carbonyl carbon appear?

options.misconception: that region holds alkyl carbons
that region holds aromatic and alkene carbons
that region holds carbons bonded to oxygen

questions.explanation: Carbonyl carbons of esters and acids are strongly deshielded and appear around 160 to 180 ppm, downfield of aromatic and oxygen-bearing carbons.
questions.hint: Carbonyl carbons are far downfield.

questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.learningObjective: Predict coupling in an ethyl group
questions.stem: An examiner asks: what splitting pattern does a CH3 group of an ethyl fragment show when adjacent to a CH2 group?

options.misconception: the methyl has neighboring protons
that is the pattern of the neighboring CH2
one neighbor would give a doublet

questions.explanation: A methyl group coupled to two equivalent methylene protons is split into a triplet by the n+1 rule, while the methylene is split into a quartet by the three methyl protons.
questions.hint: Two neighbors split the methyl into three lines.

questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: In a handout exercise, which treatment makes an O-H proton signal disappear from a proton NMR spectrum?

options.text: Adding a drop of deuterium oxide

options.misconception: heating does not remove the signal reliably
dilution shifts but does not remove the peak
field strength does not remove exchangeable signals

questions.explanation: Exchange with deuterium oxide replaces the labile O-H proton with deuterium, which is not observed in proton NMR, causing the O-H signal to vanish.
questions.hint: O-H protons exchange with deuterium.

questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: Applying the mechanism, why does bromobenzene show four signals in its proton-decoupled carbon-13 spectrum?

options.text: It contains four distinct carbon atoms only
options.misconception: bromobenzene contains six carbons

options.text: Symmetry makes the ortho, meta and para carbons equivalent in pairs
Bromine couples to only four carbons
options.misconception: bromine coupling is not observed in standard carbon-13 NMR

options.text: The ring has four different bond types
options.misconception: bond types do not determine carbon signals

questions.explanation: A mirror plane through bromine and the para carbon makes the two ortho carbons equivalent and the two meta carbons equivalent, leaving four distinct carbon environments.
questions.hint: Count unique carbons using ring symmetry.

questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: As a check, where does the OCH3 group of an aryl methyl ether typically appear in a proton NMR spectrum?

options.misconception: that is typical of an alkyl methyl
that is typical of an aldehyde
that is typical of aromatic protons

questions.explanation: Methoxy protons attached to oxygen are deshielded and usually appear as a sharp singlet near 3.7 to 3.9 ppm with no neighboring hydrogens to cause splitting.
questions.hint: Methoxy is a three-proton singlet near 3.8.

questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.learningObjective: Predict coupling in an ethyl group
questions.stem: In class discussion, what splitting pattern does a CH3 group of an ethyl fragment show when adjacent to a CH2 group?

questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: Working through the mechanism, which treatment makes an O-H proton signal disappear from a proton NMR spectrum?

questions.stem: Given the transformation, decide: why does bromobenzene show four signals in its proton-decoupled carbon-13 spectrum?

options.misconception: that is typical of an alkyl methyl
that is typical of an aldehyde
that is typical of aromatic protons

questions.explanation: Methoxy protons attached to oxygen are deshielded and usually appear as a sharp singlet near 3.7 to 3.9 ppm with no neighboring hydrogens to cause splitting.
questions.hint: Methoxy is a three-proton singlet near 3.8.

questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: Consider the reaction and decide: which proton type typically appears furthest downfield in a proton NMR spectrum?

options.misconception: alkyl methyls appear upfield near one ppm
vinyl protons appear near five to six ppm
aromatic protons appear near seven to eight ppm

questions.explanation: Carboxylic acid O-H protons are strongly deshielded and appear near ten to twelve ppm, further downfield than aromatic, vinyl or alkyl protons.
questions.hint: Acid O-H is the most deshielded common proton.

questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: Check your reasoning: a proton has two equivalent neighboring protons. How many lines does its signal show?

options.misconception: one neighbor gives a doublet
three neighbors give a quartet
no neighbors give a singlet

questions.explanation: Spin-spin coupling to n equivalent neighbors splits a signal into n plus one lines, so two equivalent neighbors give a triplet of three lines.
questions.hint: Two neighbors means n+1 equals three.

questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: In a worked example, which molecule gives exactly two signals in a proton-decoupled carbon-13 NMR spectrum?

options.misconception: pentane has three distinct carbon environments
isobutane has two carbon types with distinct methyl and methine
cyclohexane gives one carbon signal

questions.explanation: Neopentane has a central quaternary carbon and four equivalent methyl carbons, giving exactly two distinct carbon environments in the carbon-13 spectrum.
questions.hint: Symmetry reduces the number of distinct carbons.

questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: On an exam, a signal integrates to six hydrogens while another integrates to one. What does the ratio indicate?

options.misconception: integration counts protons, not environments
integration does not reveal ring size

options.text: Six equivalent protons for that environment

options.misconception: that is determined by splitting, not integration

questions.explanation: The integral of a proton NMR signal is proportional to the number of protons giving that signal, so an integral of six corresponds to six equivalent protons.
questions.hint: Integration gives relative proton counts.

questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: For the reaction under study, which distinctive signal in a proton NMR spectrum indicates an aldehyde?

options.text: A broad signal near eleven ppm
options.misconception: that suggests a carboxylic acid O-H
that suggests a terminal methyl
that suggests aromatic protons

options.text: A singlet near nine to ten ppm

questions.explanation: The aldehydic proton is strongly deshielded by the carbonyl and typically appears as a singlet around nine to ten ppm, a region relatively empty for other protons.
questions.hint: Aldehyde protons sit near nine to ten ppm.

questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: Think through the following: in which region of a carbon-13 NMR spectrum does an ester carbonyl carbon appear?

options.misconception: that region holds alkyl carbons
that region holds aromatic and alkene carbons
that region holds carbons bonded to oxygen

questions.explanation: Carbonyl carbons of esters and acids are strongly deshielded and appear around 160 to 180 ppm, downfield of aromatic and oxygen-bearing carbons.
questions.hint: Carbonyl carbons are far downfield.

questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.learningObjective: Predict coupling in an ethyl group
questions.stem: Review question: what splitting pattern does a CH3 group of an ethyl fragment show when adjacent to a CH2 group?

options.misconception: the methyl has neighboring protons
that is the pattern of the neighboring CH2
one neighbor would give a doublet

questions.explanation: A methyl group coupled to two equivalent methylene protons is split into a triplet by the n+1 rule, while the methylene is split into a quartet by the three methyl protons.
questions.hint: Two neighbors split the methyl into three lines.

questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: In a practice problem, which treatment makes an O-H proton signal disappear from a proton NMR spectrum?

options.misconception: heating does not remove the signal reliably
dilution shifts but does not remove the peak

options.text: Adding a drop of deuterium oxide

options.misconception: field strength does not remove exchangeable signals

questions.explanation: Exchange with deuterium oxide replaces the labile O-H proton with deuterium, which is not observed in proton NMR, causing the O-H signal to vanish.
questions.hint: O-H protons exchange with deuterium.

questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: When analyzing the transformation, why does bromobenzene show four signals in its proton-decoupled carbon-13 spectrum?

options.text: It contains four distinct carbon atoms only
options.misconception: bromobenzene contains six carbons

options.text: Bromine couples to only four carbons
options.misconception: bromine coupling is not observed in standard carbon-13 NMR

options.text: The ring has four different bond types
options.misconception: bond types do not determine carbon signals

options.text: Symmetry makes the ortho, meta and para carbons equivalent in pairs

questions.explanation: A mirror plane through bromine and the para carbon makes the two ortho carbons equivalent and the two meta carbons equivalent, leaving four distinct carbon environments.
questions.hint: Count unique carbons using ring symmetry.
